newsitem.title: GERMANY: German PPI rise sparks no inflation fears.
newsitem.headline: German PPI rise sparks no inflation fears.

text.p: German producer prices climbed 0.2 percent in October, but were still 0.3 percent below the level of October 1995, the Economics Ministry said Friday.
Import prices, meanwhile, were up 0.6 percent from the previous month and 1.6 percent year-on-year. Export prices were up 0.2 percent on a monthly basis, but remained unchanged year-on-year.

Economists said the data gave them no reason to expect a rise in inflation or a change in interest rates, as the producer and import price increases were linked to an increase in oil prices, and have not filtered down to consumer prices.

"This is not at all a case of inflation," said Gerhard Grebe, chief economist at Bank Julius Baer in Frankfurt. "The increase in prices is related to some increases in crude oil and heating oil prices."
Oil prices have edged up in recent weeks as cold weather crept across North America, Europe, northern Asia and Japan.
"It's nothing for the Bundesbank to worry about," added Hermann Remsperger, BHF Bank chief economist in Frankfurt.
"Prices are very favourable. Even if there is a slight increase in raw material prices, they are balanced off by restructuring in the economy and improvements in productivity."
The stable price situation also bodes well for stable interest rates, the economists said.
"We think the Bundesbank is going to stay on an unchanging course on interest rates," said Dresdner Bank economist Rolf Schneider in Frankfurt.
